extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate or beginning graduate students in complex analysis / conformal mapping
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of foundational results and explicit examples in conformal mapping: fractional linear maps, elementary conformal maps between standard domains, the Schwarz lemma and automorphisms of the disc/upper half-plane, Montel's theorem, and the Riemann mapping theorem; includes solving the Dirichlet problem in a strip via conformal maps and the Poisson integral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fractional linear transformations (Mobius maps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maps of the form z ↦ (az + b)/(cz + d) where a, b, c, d are complex numbers and the denominator is not a multiple of the numerator; often called fractional linear transformations and occur as automorphisms of the disc and upper half-plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These maps are conformal (except where denominator vanishes) and are used repeatedly to produce explicit conformal equivalences; when coefficients are real and ad − bc = 1 they give automorphisms of the upper half-plane. They can be composed and inverted using 2×2 matrix multiplication (SL2(R) / PSL2(R) viewpoint).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations and dilations as conformal maps
rubrics_metrics.description: The map z ↦ z + h (h ∈ C) and z ↦ cz (c ∈ C, c ≠ 0) are conformal maps of C to itself; if h is real the translation preserves the upper half-plane. If |c| = 1 it's a rotation; if c > 0 a dilation; if c < 0 a dilation composed with rotation by π.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use translations/rotations/dilations to move or rescale domains before applying more intricate maps; inverses are obvious (w ↦ w − h, w ↦ c⁻¹w).

rubrics_metrics.name: Power maps and sectors (z ↦ z^n, z ↦ z^α)
rubrics_metrics.description: If n is a positive integer, z ↦ z^n maps the sector {0 < arg z < π/n} conformally to the upper half-plane. More generally, for 0 < α < 2, f(z)=z^α maps the upper half-plane to the sector {0 < arg w < απ}, using a chosen branch of the logarithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose branches of log appropriately (delete a ray) to get single-valued inverses w ↦ w^{1/α}. Trace boundary behavior by following arg changes: e.g., real line pieces map to rays of given argument; composition with rotations/translations yields maps to arbitrary infinite sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map (1+z)/(1−z) from half-disc to first quadrant
rubrics_metrics.description: The map f(z) = (1 + z)/(1 − z) takes the upper half-disc { |z| < 1, Im z > 0 } conformally to the first quadrant {u > 0, v > 0}. It maps the upper half-circle to the positive imaginary axis and (−1,1) to the positive real axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute real and imaginary parts to verify image region; inverse g(w) = (w − 1)/(w + 1) maps first quadrant back into unit disc and has positive imaginary part on the quadrant. Track boundary parameterizations (z = e^{iθ}) to see how arcs map to axes (e.g., f(e^{iθ}) = i cot(θ/2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Logarithm as map from upper half-plane to strip
rubrics_metrics.description: The branch of log obtained by deleting the negative imaginary axis maps the upper half-plane to the horizontal strip {u ∈ R, 0 < v < π} via log(re^{iθ}) = log r + iθ (with −π/2 < θ < 3π/2 in the chosen branch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inverse is exponential w ↦ e^w. Trace boundary behavior: real x < 0 maps to line {· + iπ}, positive reals map to real axis, etc. Use branch cuts to control images of boundary arcs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exponential-type maps: e^{iz} mapping half-strips to half-discs
rubrics_metrics.description: The map f(z) = e^{iz} takes the half-strip { −π/2 < Re z < π/2, Im z > 0 } conformally to the half-disc { |w| < 1, Re w > 0 }, via e^{iz} = e^{−Im z} e^{i Re z}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful as inverse-step when combined with log maps; follow vertical/horizontal boundary segments to see images on circle or radii.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition principle for harmonicity (Lemma 1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F : V → U is holomorphic and u : U → C is harmonic, then u ◦ F is harmonic on V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: locally represent u as Re G for some holomorphic G on U, then G ◦ F is holomorphic on V and its real part is u ◦ F. This justifies solving Laplace/Dirichlet problems by pulling back harmonic functions via conformal maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dirichlet problem in a horizontal strip — data conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: To solve Laplace u = 0 on the horizontal strip Ω = { x + i y : x ∈ R, 0 < y < 1 } with boundary values u(x,0) = f0(x) and u(x,1) = f1(x), assume f0 and f1 are continuous and vanish at infinity (lim_{|x|→∞} f_j(x) = 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These decay conditions guarantee a continuous boundary function on the circle after conformal mapping to the unit disc and yield a unique solution vanishing at infinity. Uniqueness (for solutions vanishing at infinity) follows from standard maximum principle arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method: solve Dirichlet in strip via conformal map and Poisson integral
rubrics_metrics.description: Map the disc to the strip via explicit conformal maps F and G (given in the text) so boundary semi-circles correspond to the two lines of the strip, pull back boundary data to the circle, apply the Poisson integral on the disc, then push forward to the strip to obtain the solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit maps used: F(w) = (i/π) log((1 − w)/(1 + w)) and G(z) = (i − e^{π z})/(i + e^{π z}) (as inverses). The Poisson integral ˜u(re^{iθ}) = (1/2π) ∫ Pr(θ−φ) ˜f(e^{iφ}) dφ is applied; after change of variables one gets explicit convolution formulas for u(x,y) in terms of f0 and f1 involving kernels sin πy / (cosh πt ± cos πy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit integral formula for solution in the strip
rubrics_metrics.description: For f0, f1 continuous vanishing at infinity the harmonic solution on the strip is given by u(x,y) = (sin πy / 2) * [ ∫_{−∞}^{∞} f0(x−t)/(cosh πt − cos πy) dt + ∫_{−∞}^{∞} f1(x−t)/(cosh πt + cos πy) dt ].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This arises from pulling back the Poisson integral from the disc and performing the change of variables. In particular at y=1/2 the kernel reduces to 1/ cosh πt (self-Fourier transform property noted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Boundary-extension requirement for solving general Dirichlet via conformal map
rubrics_metrics.description: To reduce a Dirichlet problem on Ω to the disc, one needs a conformal map F^{-1}: Ω → D; to transfer boundary values, F^{-1} must extend to a continuous bijection of ∂Ω onto the unit circle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existence of a conformal map from Ω to D is given by the Riemann mapping theorem under mild hypotheses; continuous extension to the boundary requires additional regularity of ∂Ω (e.g., polygonal boundaries or other regularity conditions discussed later).

rubrics_metrics.name: Schwarz lemma (conditions and conclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f : D → D is holomorphic with f(0) = 0 then (i) |f(z)| ≤ |z| for all z ∈ D, (ii) if equality holds at some nonzero z0 then f is a rotation, and (iii) |f'(0)| ≤ 1 with equality only for rotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via power series and maximum modulus principle. Schwarz lemma is a fundamental rigidity/metric statement used to characterize automorphisms of the unit disc and to obtain sharp bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of automorphisms of the unit disc
rubrics_metrics.description: Every automorphism f of D is of the form f(z) = e^{iθ} (α − z)/(1 − ᾱ z) (the text writes α − z /(1 − α z) with |α|<1 and a rotation factor), i.e., generated by rotations and the involutive maps ψ_α(z) = (α − z)/(1 − α z).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: pick α with f(α)=0, compose with ψ_α so the resulting map fixes 0, apply Schwarz lemma to deduce it's a rotation; invert to get f. Consequence: automorphism group acts transitively on D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automorphisms of upper half-plane (SL2(R) / PSL2(R) description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aut(H) consists of maps z ↦ (a z + b)/(c z + d) where a, b, c, d are real and ad − bc = 1. Identifying M and −M gives PSL2(R), which is isomorphic to Aut(H).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check Im(f_M(z)) = (ad − bc) Im(z)/|cz + d|^2 > 0 so f_M maps H to H. Group operation corresponds to matrix multiplication; two matrices ±M give same fractional linear map so quotient to PSL2(R).

rubrics_metrics.name: Montel's theorem (normal families criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is a family of holomorphic functions on an open set Ω that is uniformly bounded on compact subsets of Ω then (i) F is equicontinuous on every compact subset, and (ii) F is a normal family (every sequence has a subsequence converging uniformly on compacts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equicontinuity follows from Cauchy estimates; normality follows from Arzela-Ascoli plus diagonalization/ exhaustion by compact sets. Definitions of uniform boundedness on compacts and equicontinuity are provided and used in proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: normal family, uniform boundedness on compacts, equicontinuity
rubrics_metrics.description: Normal: every sequence in F has a subsequence converging uniformly on compacta. Uniformly bounded on compacts: for each compact K⊂Ω there exists B s.t. |f(z)| ≤ B for all z∈K and f∈F. Equicontinuous on K: for every ε>0 ∃δ>0 such that |z−w|<δ ⇒ |f(z)−f(w)|<ε for all f∈F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the standard compactness/regularity hypotheses used to extract convergent subsequences; examples and counterexamples (real-analytic families failing equicontinuity) are discussed to motivate the holomorphic setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit of injective holomorphic functions is injective or constant (Proposition 3.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Ω is connected and {f_n} is a sequence of injective holomorphic functions on Ω converging uniformly on compacts to f, then f is either injective or constant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by contradiction uses argument principle around isolated zeros: if f(z1)=f(z2) for distinct z1,z2 then construct g_n = f_n − f_n(z1) and compare winding numbers to get contradiction because g_n are nonvanishing in small disks while limit has zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Riemann mapping theorem (existence + normalization)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Ω is a proper (nonempty, not all of C) simply connected open subset of C and z0∈Ω, then there exists a unique conformal map F:Ω→D with F(z0)=0 and F'(z0)>0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessary conditions: Ω ≠ C, connected, simply connected. Uniqueness follows from automorphisms of D fixing origin being rotations; normalization F'(z0)>0 fixes rotation. Existence proved by mapping Ω injectively into a bounded subset of D, considering family of injective maps f:Ω→D fixing 0, maximizing |f'(0)| (or |f'(z0)|), extract limit by Montel, show limit is nonconstant and injective (Proposition 3.5), then show surjectivity by a contradiction construction using automorphisms and square-root on simply connected complement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy and technical prerequisites for the Riemann mapping proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Key technical tools: exhaustion by compacts, Montel's theorem for extracting limits, Cauchy estimates to bound derivatives, Proposition 3.5 to preserve injectivity in the limit, and automorphism constructions (ψ_α) to force contradictions if limit is not surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline: embed Ω into D (Step 1), consider family F of injective maps Ω→D fixing 0 (Step 2), pick sequence that maximizes derivative at 0, extract convergent subsequence, obtain f in F with maximal derivative, and finally show f is surjective via composing with automorphisms and root branches (Step 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of Riemann's original Dirichlet-principle-based approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Riemann originally derived existence of conformal maps from solvability of the Dirichlet problem via the Dirichlet principle, but this approach requires boundary regularity and has technical difficulties (existence of minimizers, bijectivity checks, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modern proofs avoid those pitfalls; nevertheless the connection between Green's functions/Dirichlet solutions and conformal maps is conceptually important and motivates alternate constructions.
